resources.string: This box has %1$s of memory. The app buffers up to %2$d MB ahead, less when memory is short.
Lets the app size the buffer for this box and keep it in native memory, with faster seeking. Turning it on also sets the buffer and network values below for this box.
Use the values below instead of the app\'s own. When off: with ExoPlayer native memory on, the app buffers 15 to 45 s within the size it picks for this box; with it off, Media3\'s standard buffer.
Buffer ahead
How much of the film to keep ready ahead of where you are. The app keeps it topped up all the time. More helps on unsteady servers; the limit is this box\'s memory.
This box holds about %2$d s of a 4K remux and %3$d s of a web file (%1$d MB free at the last playback).
More than this box can hold for a 4K remux (about %1$d s). Lighter films still use it.
A 4K remux cannot fill this on this box (about %1$d s fit): playback starts when the memory is full.
Kept inside the Target buffer size. At %1$d MB the app keeps up to about %2$d s of it (%3$d MB at 80 Mbit/s), so at least 5 s stays ahead.
Kept inside the Target buffer size. At %1$d MB there is no room for it, so the app keeps 5 s ahead instead.

Sets the buffer from the memory this box has free when playback starts, and shrinks it when the box runs short. Turn off to pick the Target buffer size yourself: the app then keeps your size when memory runs low, and if the box really runs out, Android may close the player. On small boxes a bigger size can make playback stutter.

Memory used to buffer video ahead. The limit follows this box\'s total memory. With Managed memory budget on, the app sets the size from the memory free at playback start and shrinks the buffer while the box is short of memory.
This box has %1$s of memory. Above %2$d MB, playback may stutter.
Lets the Target buffer size go up to 2 GB. Only for boxes with 4 GB of memory or more; on smaller boxes big sizes stutter or crash.
Automatic speed-up

Helps films that keep buffering from far-away servers. The app asks the box for a bigger download window and, on boxes with enough memory, adds extra downloads if a film still runs short. Off: one standard download.
When Connections is set to a number, your own connection settings are used. Only the bigger download window still applies.
Connections
How many connections fetch a stream at once. Automatic uses one and, on boxes with enough memory, Automatic speed-up adds more when a film needs them.
Automatic
This box has %1$s of memory. More than 2 connections can make playback stutter.
Chunks smaller than 8 MB are slow on Real-Debrid and can be refused by TorBox.
Estimated memory use: about %1$d MB (buffer %2$d MB + downloads %3$d MB)
Estimated memory use: about %1$d MB (buffer %2$d MB)
